title: Three Terms and One Short Pitch
subtitle: 体育与运动 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 体育与运动（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·运动与健身）
meta: 主题语境：体育与运动（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·运动与健身）　|　核心词汇：football　|　正文 348 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 football 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1965 the coach ① kicked a football that no boy in the school would have named, and he said the kicking was the whole of the term. The ② football, meaning the ball itself and not the pitch, ran three terms and stayed unnamed in the book; a football, he said, is the only thing in a school that is judged by how long it is left unnamed.

Every ③ football in that school had the same short post beside it, and the ④ football at the far end, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A football, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to name; the coach said the naming is the part that fills three terms.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the football was the whole of the matter, meaning the American game and not the ball. The ⑥ football, meaning the American game and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody names; football, he said, is either something you kick or the only word that means both a ball and the American game. He said the American game is the part they remember.

By 1972 the ⑦ football had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short post. The ⑧ football of the whole thing, the coach wrote in October, was one school and three terms of naming; football, he said, is either the one at the far end or the reason you learned to name. He said the naming was never mentioned.

The ⑨ football I remember is the one named in the plan, which closed in 1974 and is still described as the quietest in the school. A ⑩ football, my mother said in 1976, is the only one that improves by being named; every football, she said, is the American game that has agreed to look like a ball. She said the American game was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 足球（指学校里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 足球（指那一个本身，与球场相对）
C. 固定搭配：kick a football 踢一只足球
D. n. 足球（指留给孩子们的那一个）
E. n. 足球（抽象总称，指一所学校的踢球之事）
F. n. 足球（指计划里写到、被说出名字的那一个）
G. n. 美式橄榄球（指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）
H. n. 美式橄榄球（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）

items.q: kicked a football that no boy in the school would have named
The football, meaning the ball itself and not the pitch
the football at the far end
the football was the whole of the matter
The football, meaning the American game
the football had become a line in a plan

answers.why: kick a football 意为“踢一只足球”，1965 年那位教练踢了一只学校里没有一位男孩肯说出名字的足球。
football 意为“足球”，指那一个本身而不是球场，它经过了三个学期而在簿子上没有被说出名字。
football 意为“足球”，指学校里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一根矮矮的门柱。
football 意为“足球”，指留给孩子们的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
football 意为“美式橄榄球”，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西，叔叔说这项美式橄榄球就是那件事的全部。
football 意为“美式橄榄球”，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西而不是那只足球，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
football 意为“足球”，指计划里写到、被说出名字的那一个，到 1972 年这一个成了计划里的一行。
football 意为“足球”，教练十月写道，整件事的踢球之事是一所学校和三个学期的说出名字。
football 意为“足球”，我记得的是计划里被说出名字的那一个，1974 年结束了，至今仍被说成学校里最安静的一个。
football 为抽象总称，母亲 1976 年说，一只足球是唯一会因为被好好说出名字而变得更好的东西。
